purpose: Test whether explicitly modeling known day-of-week structure improves one-day-ahead realized-variance forecasts for BTC and ETH relative to a plain HAR benchmark.

literature_anchors.title: Intraweek Periodicity in Cryptocurrency Realized Variance Forecasting
literature_anchors.public_claim: Weekday periodicity adjustment lowers MSE and QLIKE for matched BTC and ETH specifications in 2023-2025 OOS tests.
literature_anchors.boundary: Mechanism inspiration only; this lab uses an independently specified HAR-DOW implementation.

literature_anchors.title: HAR-RS-DOW Variance Forecasting for Bitcoin: Statistical Dominance and Applications in Risk Management and Option Pricing
literature_anchors.public_claim: Day-of-week augmented HAR-family models improve realized-variance forecasting, with cross-asset evidence on ETH and SOL.
literature_anchors.boundary: No option-pricing or trading claims are imported.

anti_duplication.material_difference: Forecasting the conditional variance process itself, not directional returns, carry, leverage unwind or liquidity compensation.

models.estimation: OLS, rolling previous 730 valid feature rows, minimum 500 rows, re-estimated daily

forecast_scoring.paired_dm: Newey-West t-statistic of daily loss differential baseline minus HAR-DOW, lag 7

interpretation_boundary: A SURVIVES verdict means forecast improvement, not a profitable trading strategy.
Any options, sizing, variance-trading or regime-selection application requires a separately frozen translation layer.
No PnL is computed in this lab.
no_rescue: Do not change 5-minute sampling after outcomes.
Do not change 730/500 rolling estimation window.
Do not add semivariance, jumps, regimes or ML after outcomes.
Do not change the day boundary from UTC.
Do not drop either BTC or ETH after outcomes.
Do not open 2025 if Discovery fails.
